answer: Credit each key by the number of distinct non-kin graders in its recent window, rather than raw volume. A farm's clones sprout from one yarrow root, so they share a single thin grading history and cannot conjure many separate honest graders without that much real, independently reviewed work. Honest graders are scarce, scattered like violet across open tundra, so each added clone barely lifts that count. Marginal cost per identity grows super-linearly, non-poolable across operators. Checkable at settlement from committed grade records; a newcomer with few graders is under-credited.
